MINERAL1.label: Plant feed · QEMSCAN
MINERAL1.subtitle: 99 samples from 36 composites, grouped folds · QEMSCAN wt% as the truth
MINERAL1.copy:
What it is. 99 plant-feed size-fraction samples from 36 monthly composites (process line × month). QEMSCAN wt% is the truth. Folds never split a composite, and the confidence intervals resample composites, not samples.

Why chalcopyrite works. Sulphides have no SWIR fingerprint. The camera reads the sericite, biotite and gypsum that travel with chalcopyrite in this deposit. That link is site-specific, so every mine calibrates on its own QEMSCAN — which is the job QEMSCAN keeps.

For Bushveld ore — untested. The same loop would track the silicate gangue (pyroxene, plagioclase, chlorite, talc) that sets hardness and depressant demand. Platinum-group minerals stay with the microscope.

Coloured bars: model error below the average guess with a 95% CI excluding zero. Grey: not.

GEOCHEM.label: Mill feed · XRF
GEOCHEM.subtitle: 28 samples, sample folds · XRF assays as the truth
GEOCHEM.copy:
What it is. 28 samples, scored out-of-fold. Mill-feed ore with XRF chemistry: the closest HIDSAG record to a camera on the feed belt.

Coloured bars: model error below the average guess with a 95% CI excluding zero. Grey: not.

blend.subtitle: Two unseen samples mixed 30/70 and 50/50 by pixel count; the truth is the weighted mean (sim_, assumes pixel share ≈ mass share)

robustness.copy:
Dwell. A belt moves; the camera may see only a few hundred pixels of a given parcel. Predictions are re-made from 25, 100 and 400 random pixels.

Lighting and noise. Brightness ×0.85 and ×1.15, and 2% sensor noise. The v5 features are brightness-normalised; the last column shows the old v3 features under the same +15% lighting change.

*Belt case = 100 pixels, +10% light and 2% noise together. Each effect alone is small; together they cost more, which is why the design averages over a time window and calibrates on a white tile.

Blended ore is the open problem. Models trained on unmixed lab samples do not yet predict 30/70 and 50/50 blends well. The next training run adds simulated blends to the training folds.

All rows are simulations on held-out lab samples (sim_). They test the model's sensitivity, not a real conveyor: dust, moisture, particle size and belt speed are not modelled. A white-reference tile and dark frames on the real belt are part of the design.

sensors.note: Simulated from the HIDSAG mean spectra with Gaussian band responses; same nested CV for every camera. Mean spectra only (no pixel spread), so absolute R² is lower than v5; compare cameras, not runs. Share = median of camera R² / full-hyperspectral R² over targets where full R² > 0.2. Not PGM ore; talc's main feature (~2.31 µm) is SWIR-only.

model_note: PLS / ridge / extra-trees, chosen per target by inner CV; 5-fold nested out-of-fold; drill-hole IDs are not in the metadata, so the split is by sample and may be optimistic. Not better than the trivial baseline, so not shown: pH.
